title: Integrated Finance Playbook: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, Revenue Recognition & Billing (Appendix)
author: Asha Mehta
content:
Overview

This appendix consolidates operational guidance and concrete templates for Budgeting & Forecasting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition & Billing. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, and department budget owners. Use the checklists and tables below as the authoritative operational playbook for FY2026.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood Inference legal entities and business units.
- Covers annual budgeting, quarterly rolling forecasts, procurement approvals and vendor onboarding, contract review thresholds, revenue recognition rules (ASC 606-aligned guidance), and billing/collections policies.

Key Contacts

- Finance (Budgeting & Forecasting): VP Finance (Marcus Lee) - finance@redwood.ai
- Procurement & Vendor Ops: Procurement Lead (Diego Ramirez) - procurement@redwood.ai
- Legal & Contracts: Counsel (Claire Huang) - legal@redwood.ai
- RevRec & Billing: Accounting Manager (Anita Patel) - billing@redwood.ai

1) Budgeting & Forecasting - cadence and responsibilities

Purpose: Produce an auditable, department-owned annual budget and maintain a 12-month rolling forecast that feeds company planning and cash management.

Cadence and owners:
1. Annual budget (owner: Department Head) - produced in Q4 for the next fiscal year; due to Finance by Nov 15.
2. Quarterly rolling forecast (owner: Finance with department contributions) - updated within 7 business days of quarter close.
3. Monthly variance reporting (owner: Department Manager + Finance) - distributed within 10 business days of month close.

Assumptions and scenario planning:
- All budgets must include the following assumptions: macro growth, ARR growth rates, average deal size, churn, headcount hiring plan (FTE and contractor splits), and cloud/GPU cost per unit.
- Prepare three scenarios: Base, Upside (+15% revenue / +10% margin improvement), and Downside (-10% revenue).

Variance thresholds that trigger review:
- Any line item with variance > 10% vs. budget for two consecutive months requires a written remediation plan and an executive review.

Deliverables and templates:
- Department Budget Workbook (Google Sheets template) - includes P&L roll-up, headcount plan, and capex requests.
- Forecast Model (Finance template) - supports driver-based forecasting for usage-based revenue and cost-of-goods (GPU hours, storage, networking).

2) Procurement procedures and vendor onboarding

Principles:
- Purchase requests should be submitted via the procurement portal (ProcureFlow). POs must be used for all purchases above $2,500.
- Vendor selection should balance cost, security posture, and long-term strategic value.

Vendor onboarding checklist (required for all vendors providing software or services):
- Completed Vendor Intake form in ProcureFlow.
- W-9 (or equivalent tax form) on file.
- Certificate of Insurance (COI) with minimum limits per Procurement policy.
- Security questionnaire completed if vendor will access customer data or internal systems (Security review required).
- Signed Master Services Agreement (MSA) or equivalent if cumulative spend > $50,000 or if vendor stores/processes PII.

Procurement approval matrix:
| Amount | Required Approvals |
|--------|--------------------|
| <$5,000 | Requester + Dept Manager |
| $5,000 - $50,000 | Dept Head + Finance (Procurement notified) |
| $50,001 - $250,000 | VP Finance + Procurement Lead + Legal if terms deviate |
| > $250,000 | CFO + CEO + Procurement + Legal (full contract review) |

PO creation and exceptions:
1. Requester opens a PR in ProcureFlow with justification, cost center, GL code, and vendor info.
2. Finance verifies budget availability and assigns GL code.
3. Procurement issues PO; vendor may not begin work until PO accepted unless emergency exception approved by VP Finance.
4. Exceptions: Emergency purchases (e.g., incident remediation) must be retroactively documented and approved within 5 business days by Procurement and Finance.

3) Contracts and legal process

Contract routing rules:
- All vendor agreements go through Legal. Use the Contract Intake form for initial triage.
- Standard MSA and SOW templates are the default; deviations must be documented and escalated.
- Legal review required for: any contract with indemnity or liability caps, data processing, cross-border data transfer, exclusivity, or termination for convenience clauses.

Escalation thresholds and review timelines:
- Routine reviews (standard templates, non-commercial changes): Legal SLA = 5 business days.
- Commercial negotiations or non-standard terms: Legal SLA = 10-15 business days depending on complexity.
- High-risk contracts ( > $250k, PII processing, or unusual indemnities): dedicated counsel + executive briefing within 48 hours of intake.

Contract approval matrix (also applies to customer contracts):
- Up to $100k: VP of the owning business unit + Legal sign-off.
- $100k - $500k: VP + VP Finance + Legal.
- > $500k or material changes to liability/data: CFO + Legal + CEO sign-off.

Standard clauses & negotiation playbook (summary):
- Use standard Redwood MSA: limits of liability capped at the greater of (12 months fees) or $1M unless Legal approves higher risk.
- Data protection addendum required for vendors processing customer data; reference security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention page.
- Payment and termination terms default to Net 30 unless Procurement negotiates otherwise.

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing policies (summary)

Accounting principles: Revenue recognition should follow the economic substance of the contract and align to ASC 606 (or local equivalent). Revenue is recognized when (a) performance obligations are satisfied, (b) consideration is probable, and (c) collectability is reasonably assured.

Common revenue streams and recognition treatment:
- Subscription services (hosted API): Recognize ratably over the subscription term (monthly recognition for monthly/annual prepaids). Deferred revenue recorded at invoice and amortized over service period.
- Dedicated and Private deployment contracts (capacity & installation): Separate one-time professional services (installation/setup) from ongoing capacity fees. Professional services recognized as services are delivered; if distinct, recognize separately.
- Usage-based billing (per-token / per-embedding): Recognize when usage is incurred (measure usage monthly and invoice/recognize in same period).
- Multi-element arrangements: Allocate transaction price to performance obligations based on standalone selling prices; document the allocation and rationale.

Invoicing and billing cadence:
- Standard customer billing: monthly in arrears for usage + monthly subscription fees; annual prepaids invoiced upfront and recognized over the year.
- Invoice terms: Net 30 standard. Exceptions require VP Finance approval.
- Billing disputes: Customer must notify billing@redwood.ai within 30 days of invoice issuance. Dispute SLA: acknowledge within 48 hours and resolve within 15 business days where possible.

Credit memos and refunds:
- Credit memos require Finance approval. For refunds exceeding $10,000, CFO approval required.

Collections & write-offs:
- Accounts receivable aging review weekly.
- Collections steps: 30d reminder, 60d escalation to Sales owner, 90d collections notice.
- Write-off policy: AR balances > 180 days credible & $5,000+ require CFO approval to write off; amounts below $5,000 may be written off by Accounting Manager with reconciliation.

Revenue close procedures (monthly):
1. Billing exports from billing platform (BillingOps) delivered to Accounting by day +3 after month close.
2. Deferred revenue schedules updated and reviewed by Accounting Manager (day +5).
3. Revenue recognition journal entries prepared and reviewed by VP Finance (day +7).
4. Finance posts entries and completes reconciliation by day +10.

Appendix: Common templates and snippets

- Sample contract clause (limitation of liability):
""
Except for liability arising from (i) willful misconduct, or (ii) Redwood's breach of confidentiality obligations, each party's aggregate liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (A) the fees paid or payable by Customer to Redwood in the 12 months preceding the claim, or (B) $1,000,000.
""

- Sample procurement justification (one-paragraph):
"We request to engage Vendor X for GPU runtime profiling tools to reduce inference cost per token. Projected ROI: 12 month savings of $420k against an initial subscription + integration cost of $75k. Procurement request attached with vendor security questionnaire and SOW."

- Example GL mapping guidance (summary):
- COGS (usage/GPU/inference): GL 5000 series
- R&D (model engineering, runtime): GL 6000 series
- S&M (sales commissions, GTM): GL 7000 series
- G&A (legal, finance, HR): GL 8000 series
